core_obligations: Use that F(d) is globally generated for all sufficiently large d and choose d >= m with that property (proof lines 6750-6753).

Choose a basis f_1, ..., f_r of H^0(P^n, F) and apply the multiplication lemma to write every element of H^0(P^n, F(d)) as a sum of products P_i f_i with P_i homogeneous of degree d - m (proof lines 6754-6757).
Conclude that the sections f_i generate F(m), because the sections of F(d) generate F(d) (proof lines 6758-6759).
proof_roadmap: Choose a large twist that is globally generated.
Compare sections of that twist with multiples of the base sections.
Conclude generation of the m-th twist.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that an m-regular coherent sheaf F on projective n-space has F(m) globally generated. The proof uses the standard fact that F(d) is globally generated for all sufficiently large d, chooses d >= m with that property, and picks a basis f_1, ..., f_r of H^0(P^n, F) (proof lines 6750-6754). The multiplication lemma then expresses every element of H^0(P^n, F(d)) as a sum of products P_i f_i with homogeneous P_i of degree d - m; since the sections of F(d) generate F(d), it follows that the sections f_i generate F(m) (proof lines 6755-6759). H2: the choice of the auxiliary d and the transfer of generation from the twist to the m-th twist are the substance.
